result.title: Foresight: Learning Twisted SMC for Rare Events from Reversed Relaxations
result.summary: We consider the probability that a reversible Markov chain started in a set $A$ is in a rare set $B$ after a fixed horizon, a quantity often needed for many start laws, down to single states. Twisted sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) estimates such probabilities without bias, with small variance when its proposal and twist approximate the dynamics conditioned on reaching $B$, but these components are usually learned from forward simulations, which contain almost no successful paths when the event is rare. We introduce Foresight-SMC, which learns both components from the target side: under reversibility, relaxations started in $B$ that return to $A$ are, read backwards, exact samples of the conditioned paths, and their number is governed by the return probability rather than by the rare probability. Extending this reversal to the recorded propose--accept decisions of a Metropolis-adjusted sampler, we fit a controlled Langevin proposal with exact likelihood ratios by maximum likelihood, together with a classifier twist; the resulting estimator is unbiased for any start law. A variance analysis shows that resampling reduces the variance when the importance weights degenerate, as they do over long horizons. On an Allen--Cahn field, the learned proposal alone suffices, and one trained model is more accurate than splitting at equal cost. On alanine tripeptide, resampling with the learned twist is necessary, and Foresight-SMC needs less computation per query than adaptive multilevel splitting on localized start sets.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Foresight-SMC：利用可逆链下自目标集出发、返回起点的松弛路径反向获得条件路径的精确样本，据此以最大似然学习受控 Langevin 提议与分类器 twist，从而对任意起始分布无偏地估计稀有事件概率，并给出方差分析与两类物理系统实验。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽无视觉或多模态内容，但其「成功路径极罕见时从目标侧反向学习 twist 与提议」的思路，可能与 LVR 中推理轨迹训练的监督与贡献分配、逐步中间状态引导及重采样/停止策略有可供核查的概念联系。
